newsitem.title: FINLAND: IVO says merger with Neste unlikely - paper.
newsitem.headline: IVO says merger with Neste unlikely - paper.

text.p: A merger between Finnish state-owned power producer Imatran Voima (IVO) and oil, energy and chemicals group Neste is far less likely than what people have been led to believe, IVO CEO Heikki Marttinen was quoted as saying in daily Helsingin Sanomat on Thursday.
"The likelihood of a merger is substantially smaller than what people have been led to believe since the launch of the review by the trade and industry ministry," Marttinen said.

"I believe that ... as a result of the study, areas of co-operation and options somewhere in between will be found, based on which we can proceed towards sensible solutions from the point of view of energy policy and the markets," he said.
The ministry said on Tuesday it would undertake a review to "evaluate the options for broadening the shareholder base and the structural alternatives for joint development of the two companies."
The state owns 84 percent of Neste and all of IVO. A partial floatation of IVO has been expected. Neste President Jukka Viinanen said a merger was one option under investigation.
